answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with a time delta: new agents start near zero trust and earn weight only after sustained, verifiable work, so spinning up thousands of fresh identities buys nothing on day one. Like umber pigment darkening slowly as layers build, reputation must accumulate gradually and decay when idle. Add a quartz-like hardness test: each agent periodically proves useful work tied to its own history, so running a sybil army costs more per identity than honest participation.
